_comment: MovieHouse — what changed, per release. The app reads the copy of this file in the public repo sourov-cmd/moviehouse-releases (raw.githubusercontent), because the app's own repo is private. COPY RULES (owner, 2026-09-08): this page is read by real users, so write like a product, not like a changelog to the developer — no internal words (admin, endpoint, fallback), no confessing old bugs, no Bengali (the whole app UI is English), one benefit per line, present tense. Update this file, mirror it to the public repo, and keep app_config.release_notes in the same voice.

highlights.title: Sign in on TV from your phone
highlights.body: In My Space, tap Sign in on TV, point the camera at the code on your TV and tap once. Your TV signs in as you, with nothing to type on the remote.

highlights.title: Any camera works
highlights.body: Scan the TV's code with your phone's own camera or any scanner and MovieHouse opens on the right page. Without the app, the same code opens a web page to sign in.

highlights.title: Type the code instead
highlights.body: No camera at hand? Enter the eight characters shown on the TV on the same page.

highlights.title: Room for your TV
highlights.body: If your account is already on its full number of devices, the page lists them so you can free one and the TV signs in right after.

highlights.title: The TV code is yours alone
highlights.body: A TV's sign-in code works only while its sign-in page is open, and only one code is live per TV. Leave the page and it is cancelled at once.

highlights.title: MovieHouse on TV, one tap away
highlights.body: The TV card in Every screen now has Sign in on TV right at the top, next to the download address and install steps.

highlights.title: View downloads takes you straight there
highlights.body: Tap View downloads on a title, from the floating window or the full page, and you land on your Downloads shelf at once, with the film still playing in its window.

highlights.title: Skip ripples stay inside the picture
highlights.body: Double tap to skip in the small window and the ripple stays within the video, never over the page below it.

highlights.title: MovieHouse on TV and other screens
highlights.body: In My Space, see every screen MovieHouse runs on: the TV app with its download address and install steps, and the ones coming next.

highlights.title: The TV link, one tap away
highlights.body: Copy moviehouse.bond/tv from the TV card and paste it into your TV's browser or Downloader app. The install steps are right below it.

highlights.title: Privacy Policy, Terms and Copyright in the app
highlights.body: Read them in My Space under About, without leaving the app.

highlights.title: Every channel in one place
highlights.body: Telegram, YouTube, TikTok, Facebook and email support, each one tap away in Share & help, with the website right below.

highlights.title: Updates arrive as a pop-up
highlights.body: A new version shows up as a card over the page you are on, with what changed and one Update button. If the installer is closed by mistake, press Install to open it again.

highlights.title: Tap a title and it plays
highlights.body: The film starts right on its page, with episode chips, the season list and the audio language all one tap away. Continue watching and Watch history open the same way, on the episode and second you left.

highlights.title: A floating window
highlights.body: Press Back or Home and the film keeps playing in a small window you can move. Tap it to return to the same second.

highlights.title: Choose your picture quality
highlights.body: Every quality a title really has, each with its size, and the one you pick stays sharp.

highlights.title: Download films and series
highlights.body: Pick the quality and language, see the size before you start, and watch offline in the small player or full screen.

highlights.title: Download subtitles for any title
highlights.body: In the player, open Subtitles, then Download subtitle. Pick a language, tap a file, and it switches on and stays with the title.

highlights.title: Clips made for swiping
highlights.body: Swipe up for the next video, and starting a clip pauses anything else that was playing.

highlights.title: Cleaner gesture controls
highlights.body: Volume, brightness, double tap and 2x speed show a smooth white look, with a gentle tap at the ends.

highlights.title: My List, alerts and smarter search
highlights.body: Keep your picks in My List, hear about new episodes, and search that remembers what you asked.

highlights.title: Keep watching, hands free
highlights.body: Series play on with an Up next countdown, and sound keeps going in the background when you want it.

highlights.title: More in My Space
highlights.body: Continue watching, Share MovieHouse, and help on Telegram and Facebook. Sign out asks first.

highlights.title: Download subtitles for any title
highlights.body: In the player, open Subtitles, then Download subtitle. Pick a language, tap a file, and it switches on and stays with the title.

highlights.title: Cleaner gesture controls
highlights.body: Volume, brightness, double tap and 2x speed now show a smooth white look, with a gentle tap at the ends.

highlights.title: Swipe up in Clips
highlights.body: A quick hint shows how to swipe up for the next video the first time you open Clips.

highlights.title: More in My Space
highlights.body: Continue watching, counts for your library, Share MovieHouse, and help on Telegram and Facebook. Sign out now asks first.

highlights.title: One sound at a time
highlights.body: Starting a clip pauses the video that was playing, and your subtitle size now applies everywhere.

highlights.title: Subtitles saved with your downloads
highlights.body: Pick one or more subtitle languages in the Download sheet. They are saved with the video and play without internet.

highlights.title: A fresh My Space
highlights.body: Your account, My List, downloads and the space they use, all in one card, with neatly grouped options.

highlights.title: My List that keeps your picks
highlights.body: Tap Add to list on any movie or series and find it again under My List, on every phone you sign in to.

highlights.title: A smarter search box
highlights.body: The search box suggests what people are watching right now. Tap Search to look it up, or type your own.

highlights.title: Search remembers what you asked
highlights.body: Recent searches are kept the moment you press Search, fold neatly, and clear only after you confirm.

highlights.title: Popular picks in your notifications
highlights.body: See today's hot movies and series in one notification and open any of them with a tap. Swipe it away any time.

highlights.title: Keep listening in the background
highlights.body: Turn on Background play in Settings to keep the sound going with the screen off, with play, pause, skip 10 seconds, next episode and a progress bar in your notifications.

highlights.title: New episode alerts
highlights.body: Series in My List tell you when a new episode arrives.

highlights.title: Settings that do what they say
highlights.body: Wi-Fi only streaming, Data saver, Streaming quality and Delete finished downloads now work everywhere, including the floating window.

highlights.title: Up next, counted down
highlights.body: In the last seconds of an episode a card in the corner shows what plays next, even the next season. Tap Play to start it now or close the card to stay.

highlights.title: Series play on by themselves
highlights.body: The next episode now starts by itself on the small player and in the floating window too, not only in full screen.

highlights.title: Whole posters in search
highlights.body: Search results and Top Searches show the full poster, nothing cut off.

highlights.title: Fit, Fill or Stretch
highlights.body: The picture button switches between the whole picture, a screen-filling crop and a full stretch, with a small label that says which one is on.

highlights.title: Your language stays with you
highlights.body: Pick a different audio in full screen and it is still the one playing when you go back to the small screen or the floating window.

highlights.title: Skipping in the window is smoother
highlights.body: Jumping back 10 seconds in the floating window plays at once, and a small spinner shows whenever the film is loading.

highlights.title: Settings that let you see the film
highlights.body: Audio, Quality, Subtitles and Speed now open on a see-through panel, so the picture stays in view while you choose.

highlights.title: Share a title with a real link
highlights.body: Share sends a link to the title. Friends with MovieHouse land right on it; everyone else gets a page to download the app.

highlights.title: Home works even offline
highlights.body: With no internet, Home still shows the shelves you last saw, with a quick Retry. Your downloads are one tap away.

highlights.title: Downloads play in the small screen and the window
highlights.body: A downloaded film opens on its own page with the small player, goes full screen in a tap and keeps playing in the floating window.

highlights.title: Posters on your downloads, offline too
highlights.body: Every download keeps its own poster on your phone, so your list is easy to recognise with no internet.

highlights.title: A friendlier first-time guide
highlights.body: The gesture guide now appears on the small player, where every film starts, and you can skip it any time.

highlights.title: Storage checked before you download
highlights.body: If your phone is short on space, MovieHouse tells you before the download starts instead of failing halfway.

highlights.title: The film shrinks straight into its window
highlights.body: Going back from a film now shrinks the picture you are watching into the floating window, with no blank or dark screen on the way.

highlights.title: MovieHouse stays fully yours underneath
highlights.body: While the window floats, every page, tab and poster behind it scrolls and opens as usual, and the window stays with the picture wherever you drag it.

highlights.title: A dropped signal no longer closes the window
highlights.body: If your connection blinks while the window floats, the film waits, reconnects on its own and plays on from the same moment.

highlights.title: Every window button works, everywhere
highlights.body: Play, pause, the 10-second skips, full screen and close answer at once, inside the app and outside it.

highlights.title: Back to the same second
highlights.body: Opening the window full size returns you to the same page and the same moment, with nothing to load again.

highlights.title: Search keeps out of the way
highlights.body: The keyboard tucks away as soon as you open a result, so the floating window sits where it belongs.

highlights.title: The floating window stays a window
highlights.body: The small window keeps to its own corner of the screen, so the page behind it scrolls and opens exactly as it always does while your film plays on.

highlights.title: Its buttons sit on the picture
highlights.body: Play, pause and the two 10-second skips are drawn on the film itself, wherever the window is and whatever shape the film is.

highlights.title: Home always floats the film
highlights.body: Leaving MovieHouse with a film running puts it in the floating window every time, however you got there.

highlights.title: The floating window's buttons answer everywhere
highlights.body: Pause, play and the two 10-second skips on the floating window now work wherever you are — on your home screen, in another app, or with MovieHouse open behind the window.

highlights.title: The window shows what the film is doing
highlights.body: The middle button turns into play the moment you pause the film, and back into pause when it runs again.

highlights.title: One floating window, inside the app and outside it
highlights.body: The small window that appears when you leave a film is now Android's own floating window wherever you are — the same size, the same controls, draggable anywhere — and MovieHouse stays open behind it, so you can keep browsing while the film plays.

highlights.title: Closing the window hands the page back
highlights.body: Close the floating window and the title you were on picks up its own film from the second you left it.

highlights.title: Every copy now shows the size it really is
highlights.body: Quality lists carry every size a title offers, from every kind of server, so nothing is hidden behind a single entry any more.

highlights.title: The size you are watching is defended
highlights.body: If a server starts to struggle, MovieHouse looks for the same picture size somewhere else first and only steps down when no copy anywhere still has it.

highlights.title: Change one thing and only that changes
highlights.body: Picking another audio language or another size keeps the second you are on and everything else you chose.

highlights.title: Moving between screens loads nothing
highlights.body: Full screen, the small player and the floating window are one playback: every move between them keeps playing without a pause.

highlights.title: The quality list is what the film really has
highlights.body: Every size in the Quality list is read from the stream itself, so there are no odd numbers like 816P any more, nothing is offered that cannot actually play, and the size on the control bar and the size in the list are always the same one.

highlights.title: Audio is a language, not a server
highlights.body: The Audio list now names languages and nothing else, the language you are hearing is marked, and picking one takes the best copy of it that MovieHouse can reach at that moment.

highlights.title: The size you chose is defended
highlights.body: If the copy you are watching starts to struggle, MovieHouse looks for the same picture size elsewhere first and only makes the picture smaller when no copy anywhere still has it.

highlights.title: Nothing reloads on the way between screens
highlights.body: Full screen, the small player, the floating window inside the app and the one over your home screen are all the same playback now. Moving between them keeps the second you are on, and the audio language you chose comes back with you.

highlights.title: A title you tap always starts
highlights.body: Opening another film while the small floating window is playing now closes the window and starts what you asked for.

highlights.title: One row per server
highlights.body: The server list no longer repeats the same copy twice, and it says plainly which one is playing.

highlights.title: Full quality, and it stays there
highlights.body: Films and episodes now open at the sharpest picture the library has and hold it, instead of settling for a soft one. MovieHouse asks the video service for several parts of a film at the same time, which is what makes the difference.

highlights.title: No more stopping in the middle
highlights.body: Playback keeps a deep reserve of video ahead of you, so a dip in your connection no longer turns into a pause every minute. If a copy still struggles, MovieHouse quietly moves to another copy of the same film from the exact second you had reached.

highlights.title: The home page fills even on a slow connection
highlights.body: Shelves that used to come up empty when the network hesitated now keep asking until they have their posters, so the page fills instead of staying dark.

highlights.title: Surround sound where the film has it
highlights.body: When a film is published with a 5.1 soundtrack, MovieHouse can now fall back to that copy, so you hear the full mix rather than plain stereo.

highlights.title: Films open in seconds
highlights.body: Tapping play now shows the picture straight away instead of waiting while the app looks around for a server. On a slow line a film that used to take about eleven seconds to appear now starts in about four.

highlights.title: Smooth first, sharp right after
highlights.body: Playback begins on a copy your connection can carry and climbs to the sharpest one once it knows your speed, so a film keeps running instead of freezing every few seconds.

highlights.title: The language you picked is the language you get
highlights.body: Choosing Hindi, Tamil, Telugu or the original audio now decides which copy is played, so a film no longer opens in another dub because a different server answered first.

highlights.title: One floating window
highlights.body: The small window inside the app is now exactly the window Android gives you outside the app — same size, same shape — so a film looks the same wherever you keep watching it.

highlights.title: Your language stays your language
highlights.body: Pick Hindi, Tamil, Telugu or the original audio and the film stays there. If one copy will not play, the next copy of the same language takes over, and the title tells you plainly when a language has nothing left to try.

highlights.title: Films start sooner
highlights.body: A title is now looked up once and the answer is shared by the page, the small player and full screen, so the picture arrives noticeably faster on a slow line.

highlights.title: The sharp stream is given time to start
highlights.body: The adaptive stream is no longer dropped while it is still filling, so more films open on the sharpest copy and stay there.

highlights.title: A cleaner quality list
highlights.body: The quality list shows 480P, 720P and 1080P as the film really carries them, with one of them marked as the one you are watching.

highlights.title: Pick your picture quality
highlights.body: Tap the quality button while a film is playing and choose 480P, 720P or 1080P. The film keeps playing from the same second, in the same language, with your subtitles and your speed untouched.

highlights.title: Films open faster
highlights.body: Titles now open on the library's own adaptive stream, so the picture arrives in a moment and climbs to the best quality your line can carry.

highlights.title: Back leaves you on the title, still watching
highlights.body: Coming out of full screen puts the film straight back into the player on the title page, playing on. Leaving by the phone's Home button still floats it over everything else.

highlights.title: One floating window
highlights.body: The window inside the app is the same shape and carries the same three controls as the one over your home screen, and tapping it opens the film exactly where you left it.

highlights.title: The main page keeps your place
highlights.body: Open a title from any shelf and come back: the page is where you were, and every shelf is still scrolled to the poster you had reached.

highlights.title: Nothing plays behind you
highlights.body: Leave a title before the picture appears and it stops there, with no sound following you out of the page.

highlights.title: Films download now
highlights.body: Tapping Download on a film starts it and keeps it going to the end. Films are served from a host that had been refusing the app's requests, and it no longer does.

highlights.title: Sizes you can trust
highlights.body: Every row now shows the size the library itself publishes for that exact quality and audio, so what the sheet says is what the library says.

highlights.title: A size on every quality
highlights.body: 720P and 1080P rows carry their size as well, not only their length.

highlights.title: Only the qualities that exist
highlights.body: The quality tabs are the ones the library really holds for that title, so a tab can no longer open onto an empty row.

highlights.title: Downloads finish
highlights.body: A download now runs straight through to the end instead of stopping with a server message: the app no longer sends the one request header this video host refuses.

highlights.title: Every quality is really there
highlights.body: Each episode and each film is offered at every quality the library holds for it, from all of its sources at once, so a row no longer says a quality is unavailable when it is.

highlights.title: Sizes and lengths, straight away
highlights.body: Rows fill in with the real size and length — 249.8MB | 57:22 — and a row never sits on “checking size…”: if a quality carries no published size, its length is shown and nothing is invented.

highlights.title: Films download too
highlights.body: A film whose first source answers with nothing is now offered from the others, with its real size, instead of showing an empty sheet.

highlights.title: Every quality a series really has
highlights.body: The Download sheet now offers each episode at every resolution the library publishes for it — 480p included — instead of only the one it happened to hand over first.

highlights.title: How big it is, on every row
highlights.body: Each episode shows its real size and its length, like 149.3MB | 57:22, and the numbers stay put when you switch quality or audio.

highlights.title: A season dropdown
highlights.body: A series with several seasons gets a Season picker beside the language, and its rows are numbered S01 E01 so you always know what you are saving.

highlights.title: Nothing covers the picture
highlights.body: The audio and season sheets on the watch page now open under the video like the Download sheet, and scroll inside themselves.

highlights.title: Downloads keep their artwork offline
highlights.body: A saved film keeps its poster on the phone, so the Downloads shelf looks right with no network — older downloads pick theirs up too.

highlights.title: Downloads that really start
highlights.body: Tap Download and the film starts saving straight away, with a progress notification while it works and one line when it is done.

highlights.title: A whole season to choose from
highlights.body: A series now opens on its own episode list at every quality the library carries, so you can pick the episodes you want and see what each one weighs.

highlights.title: The language beside the title follows your audio
highlights.body: Switch the audio and the title says that language, on the page, in the Download sheet and on the file you saved.

highlights.title: The Download sheet sits under the picture
highlights.body: It opens right below the video and never covers it, and a long episode list scrolls inside it. The quality tabs read cleanly, 1080P included.

highlights.title: What you pick is what you get
highlights.body: The quality and the language you tap are the ones saved, and the Downloads shelf states both.

highlights.title: The picture stays when you come back from full screen
highlights.body: Leaving the full screen player used to hand the small player a blank picture while the sound carried on. The film stays on screen now.

highlights.title: Changing the audio on the small player really changes it
highlights.body: Picking a language on the small player now plays that language, the same as it already did on the full screen.

highlights.title: The Audio list appears on the full screen too
highlights.body: Titles that offer several languages now show the Audio button on the full screen player, with every language the library carries.

highlights.title: The download list now carries every language
highlights.body: Titles opened from the film shelves were asking for their servers with the wrong number, so the list arrived empty and only a couple of servers were offered. They now ask with the right one, and the full language list appears.

highlights.title: Every language a film has, in the download list
highlights.body: The download list now gathers the servers from every place that knows them, so a title with ten languages is not shown as two.

highlights.title: The download moves on when a server will not answer
highlights.body: If the server you are on cannot be read, the next one is tried by itself, so a download no longer depends on the first server alone.

highlights.title: Every language the film has is offered
highlights.body: The download list now shows all of a film's servers, so a Hindi or Tamil soundtrack is never left out of the choices.

highlights.title: The download starts on the language you opened
highlights.body: Opening a film in a language now starts the download from that language's own server, instead of whichever one came first.

highlights.title: The picture at the top keeps its whole frame
highlights.body: A square poster is shown in a square space, so the artwork you see is the whole artwork that was made.

highlights.title: The next poster shows beside the one you are on
highlights.body: The moving row at the top of ShortTV now shows the edge of the next picture on each side, so it is clear there is more and a swipe has somewhere to go.

highlights.title: The band above the picture belongs to the picture
highlights.body: The strip behind the clock and the tabs now takes its colour from the poster it sits above, so the top of the page reads as one picture instead of showing the same image twice.

highlights.title: Mini TV in Bengali plays in Bengali
highlights.body: Every Mini TV language row now carries titles in that language only, and the row keeps itself full as you scroll.

highlights.title: Shorts open with a short
highlights.body: A title joins the shorts feed with a clip that really is a short, so the feed keeps moving and nothing disappears from it.

highlights.title: The Mini TV rows stay together
highlights.body: The language rows keep their place as one block on the ShortTV tab.

highlights.title: The band above the picture now belongs to the picture
highlights.body: The strip behind the clock, the search box and the tabs is drawn from the page that is actually showing, so it changes with the artwork instead of keeping the first one.

highlights.title: Only the shorts rows you asked for
highlights.body: On the front page a row of shorts is drawn only for the shelves you named. Everything else shows the ordinary row of posters it always was.

highlights.title: Back stays with the player
highlights.body: Coming back from a full-screen video keeps the film in the floating window. The page underneath no longer starts a different video of its own, so Back stops putting the previous title back on screen.

highlights.title: The ShortTV tab is back
highlights.body: ShortTV carries its own tab again with every category it offers, including the Mini TV rows for Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam and Kannada.

highlights.title: The bar sits on the picture itself
highlights.body: The strip behind the clock, the search box and the category tabs now carries the top of the page's own artwork, softened, exactly as the picture reaches it.

highlights.title: And nothing covers the picture
highlights.body: The sharp artwork still begins below the bar and the tabs, so nothing is drawn across it.

highlights.title: Language pages move by hand
highlights.body: The big picture on the Hindi, Bengali, Tamil and Telugu pages can now be swiped, and small dots underneath show how many there are.

highlights.title: Back returns to the floating player
highlights.body: Leaving a full-screen video with Back now shrinks it into the floating window instead of closing it, on every player page.

highlights.title: Only the shorts you asked for
highlights.body: The home page keeps just the short shelves you named, in the order they appear today; everything else stays exactly where it was.

highlights.title: A ShortTV tab of its own
highlights.body: ShortTV now has its own tab carrying every category it offers, including the Mini TV rows for Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam and Kannada.

highlights.title: The whole picture, edge to edge
highlights.body: The big picture at the top of the home page now shows the full frame, all the way to both sides, exactly as it was made.

highlights.title: Nothing hidden behind the bar
highlights.body: The artwork begins below the search box and the category tabs, so the clock, the search box and the tabs stay easy to read and nothing is drawn across the picture.

highlights.title: Posters show in full
highlights.body: Posters on the home page now fit their card, so no title loses the sides of its artwork.

highlights.title: Shorts right on the home page
highlights.body: Tap a shorts shelf and Clips opens on it straight away; Back puts you back exactly where you were on the home page.

highlights.title: Back returns to the floating player
highlights.body: After watching several films in a row, Back tucks the one you were watching into the small window instead of stepping back through the ones before it.

highlights.title: Shorts play again
highlights.body: Every clip opens and plays, and the next one follows on its own.

highlights.title: The front page moves by itself
highlights.body: The big picture at the top of the home page changes on its own, so what is newest is always in front of you.

highlights.title: The picture runs to the very top
highlights.body: Artwork now rises behind the clock and melts into the page below it, with the title and its small poster sitting underneath.

highlights.title: Nothing hides the picture
highlights.body: Full screen stays full screen in Shorts, including while you change quality, speed or captions.

highlights.title: Shorts that play again
highlights.body: The clips feed asks for its six titles more patiently and, if a batch still comes back empty, asks again one at a time the way the build that worked did — so a slow line can no longer turn into an empty feed. A clip that will not start still steps down a quality rather than waiting for ever.

highlights.title: One floating window, twice
highlights.body: The window inside the app and the one outside it are now drawn from a single definition, so they carry the same three actions in the same places instead of looking like two different things.

highlights.title: The page behind the picture
highlights.body: The small screen and the player now sit on the same near-black their own app uses, so the picture and the page around it belong together.

highlights.title: The poster at the top, as it should be
highlights.body: The name sits under the poster instead of across it, the artwork clears the status bar, and the billboard can be swiped by hand — a finger also stops the rotation so it cannot pull the page back mid-swipe.

highlights.title: Shorts that start, or say why
highlights.body: The feed now asks for six titles at a time instead of one, a file that will not begin steps down a quality or is passed over, and a feed with nothing in it says so and offers Try again.

highlights.title: One player for both screens
highlights.body: Going full screen and coming back does not load anything again: the film you are watching simply moves to the other screen.

highlights.title: The small picture does everything the big one does
highlights.body: Swipe across it to move through the film from exactly where you are, hold it down for double speed, and the volume and brightness read-outs sit in the middle of the picture.

highlights.title: A window you can move, and a widget with real posters
highlights.body: The floating window inside the app drags anywhere on the screen, and the home-screen widget carries four of your own posters with a search line above them.

highlights.title: Download subtitles
highlights.body: Search subtitles by name, switch one on straight away, and save it to your phone as a .srt file you can keep.

highlights.title: MovieHouse on your home screen
highlights.body: A widget of our own: search and shorts one tap away, offered the first time you open the app.

highlights.title: Shorts in a floating window
highlights.body: A short keeps playing over your home screen in a tall window its own shape, with the same controls films have.

highlights.title: Nothing cut off, nothing stretched
highlights.body: Films now play exactly as the file is by default; trimming the black edges is a choice in Settings.

highlights.title: Films at their real shape
highlights.body: Every picture keeps its own proportions on the watch page and in the floating window, with clean black edges instead of a stretched frame.

highlights.title: One floating window, everywhere
highlights.body: The same window with the same controls inside the app and over your home screen, from the small player and from full screen alike.

highlights.title: The language the title promises
highlights.body: A title marked [Hindi] opens its Hindi copy, and the audio menu names what you are really hearing.

highlights.title: Full quality on a fast line
highlights.body: Films are no longer held to your screen size: the best picture the server has plays when your connection can carry it.

highlights.title: Clips are short again
highlights.body: The swipe feed keeps to real shorts in your own language, with a slim progress line like the rest of the app.

highlights.title: A calmer home page
highlights.body: Shorts shelves live in Clips, and the page itself is a softer dark grey.

highlights.title: Every episode on offer really plays
highlights.body: The episode list follows the audio language you pick, so what you tap is what the library actually has.

highlights.title: A clear word when something is not there yet
highlights.body: If a season or an episode has not arrived, the page says so instead of blaming your connection.

highlights.title: A watch page that starts watching
highlights.body: Tap a poster and the film begins right there, with the name, the facts and the episodes under it — no page in between.

highlights.title: The picture stays where it belongs
highlights.body: Scroll the page and the film stays pinned at the top, still playing, with no reload.

highlights.title: Small screen, full control
highlights.body: Brightness, volume, scrubbing and double-tap skip all work on the small picture, exactly as they do on the full screen.

highlights.title: One film, one position
highlights.body: Move between the small picture, the full screen and the floating window and the film carries on from the same second, every time.

highlights.title: Back keeps playing
highlights.body: Leaving the page shrinks the film into a floating window inside the app, and pressing Home floats it over your phone.

highlights.title: Language and season, their own way
highlights.body: Pick an audio language or a season from a sheet that rises from the bottom, and the film continues in the new language from the same second.

highlights.title: Hundreds more episodes play
highlights.body: Titles and episodes that used to stop with an error now open, including short serials and the ones that only had a second copy.

highlights.title: Shorts in your own language
highlights.body: Clips opens with shorts from your own country first, then the languages nearest you, then the rest of the world.

highlights.title: Best quality from the first second
highlights.body: Films open at the best picture your connection carries, and the quality button shows the size you are actually watching.

highlights.title: Audio that tells the truth
highlights.body: The language shown is the language playing, a title in your language opens in it, and only tracks that really exist are offered.

highlights.title: Downloads you can recognise
highlights.body: Every download keeps its own artwork, so your list looks right even with no connection.

highlights.title: A watch page that starts watching
highlights.body: Tap a poster and the film begins right there, with the name, the facts and the episodes under it — no page in between.

highlights.title: Hundreds more episodes play
highlights.body: Titles and episodes that used to stop with an error now open, including short serials and the ones that only had a second copy.

highlights.title: Best quality from the first second
highlights.body: Films open at the best picture your connection carries, and the quality button shows the size you are actually watching.

highlights.title: Audio that tells the truth
highlights.body: The language shown is the language playing, a title in your language opens in it, and only tracks that really exist are offered.

highlights.title: Shorts in your own language
highlights.body: Clips now opens with shorts from your country first, then the rest of the world.

highlights.title: Downloads you can recognise
highlights.body: Every download keeps its own artwork, so your list looks right even with no connection.

highlights.title: Episodes in numbered chips
highlights.body: Pick a season and tap an episode number — the whole season fits on one line.

highlights.title: A floating window
highlights.body: Shrink a film into a small window and keep watching while you use the phone.

highlights.title: Home stays where you left it
highlights.body: Category strips, poster rows and sorting all hold their place, including after you come back from a title.

highlights.title: Posters that appear at once
highlights.body: Artwork now arrives sized for your screen, so a page fills in a blink instead of loading in pieces — and it holds up on a slow connection.

highlights.title: Every collection opens in full
highlights.body: Tap a collection's name and you get everything in it, page after page, with For You, Latest and Rating to sort by.

highlights.title: A wide, moving cover at the top
highlights.body: Home, Movies and Series open on the library's own wide artwork, and the search, alerts and tabs above it stay readable over every picture.

highlights.title: Search that finishes your words
highlights.body: Suggestions appear as you type, chips narrow a search to films, series, shorts, music, sports or learning, and results keep loading as you scroll.

highlights.title: Music search that finds music
highlights.body: A song search now answers with songs — pages of them, by title or by artist.

highlights.title: Clips, the way a short feed should be
highlights.body: One story at a time with its poster and its clock, a heart to react with, a back arrow of its own, and no bar covering the controls. Like a story and the next episode follows.

highlights.title: You come back where you left
highlights.body: Leaving a title, a search or a clip returns you to the same place on the same row.

highlights.title: Easier on your battery
highlights.body: Leave the app while something is playing and it pauses instead of running on, and pictures are streamed no larger than your screen can show.

highlights.title: Short serials that play
highlights.body: The vertical short serials — the Hot Short TV collection and the rest — now open with their whole episode list, 40 or more episodes each, in up to 1080p, and they download like anything else.

highlights.title: Ask for what is not out yet
highlights.body: A title that has not been released carries no Play or Download button any more. It carries the date it is expected and a Request button, and you can see how many people have asked for it.

highlights.title: Clips closer to home
highlights.body: The short feed now starts with the serials the library is featuring, so what you swipe through includes Indian stories and not only foreign ones.

highlights.title: Every category the library has
highlights.body: Each tab now carries all of its own collections, read fresh as you open it — so a new collection appears the day it does, and each one pages as deep as it goes.

highlights.title: New tabs: Education, Cricket, Football, Game
highlights.body: Four more sections join Home, FightZone and Midnight, each filled from the library's own listings.

highlights.title: Hindi, Tamil and Telugu of their own
highlights.body: Language tabs now hold titles in that language, not a copy of Trending.

highlights.title: Music, rebuilt as a music app
highlights.body: Charts, genre chips, quick picks with running times and its own search — and a song still opens in the player you already know, with its audio tracks and subtitles.

highlights.title: One card per title
highlights.body: A film with five language editions is one card again, with the languages inside the player's Audio menu, and posters carry their language mark.

highlights.title: 18+ stays where it belongs
highlights.body: Midnight keeps its own collections, and adult titles no longer appear on ordinary shelves or in ordinary results.

highlights.title: Kinder to your battery
highlights.body: A download that cannot continue now waits for you instead of retrying in the background.

highlights.title: A calmer top of the screen
highlights.body: The bar starts clear over the day's big title and settles into black as you scroll, with a search box and notifications right at the top of every tab.

highlights.title: Opens on the new home, every time
highlights.body: The app now keeps its own copy of the home layout, so it starts straight on the new pages — even offline.

highlights.title: FightZone and Midnight
highlights.body: Wrestling gets a tab of its own, and the 18+ section becomes Midnight with its named collections — UllU, Vivamax, and more — each one paging as deep as it goes.

highlights.title: Search that knows the whole library
highlights.body: Results arrive from everywhere at once, split into All, Movies and Series, and titles that only ever lived in one corner of the catalogue now turn up too.

highlights.title: Filters on every category
highlights.body: Open any category and refine it by genre, country, year, language and sort — the same choices the library itself offers.

highlights.title: Better first seconds of playback
highlights.body: Films open at their real quality instead of easing up from blurry, audio menus name their languages properly, and subtitles reach many more titles — including Clips.

highlights.title: One title, one poster
highlights.body: A film no longer appears once per language on the shelves, and each poster carries a small mark for its audio language.

highlights.title: Lighter on the phone
highlights.body: Caches now clean up after themselves, and a Clear cache switch in Settings frees space whenever you want — downloads stay untouched.

highlights.title: A main page arranged like the library itself
highlights.body: Eleven tabs across the top — Movies, Series, Anime, Indian, Bengali, Languages, Kids, Sports, Game — holding 134 categories, each one a real slice of the catalogue rather than a fixed list.

highlights.title: Categories that do not stop
highlights.body: Swipe a shelf and it keeps bringing titles until that category runs out. A category page that used to stall after a few rows now carries on by itself.

highlights.title: Names under the posters
highlights.body: Every card shows its title on one line, shortened with … when it is long, so nothing has to be recognised by its artwork alone.

highlights.title: Clips
highlights.body: Short films in a full-screen feed you flick through, playing by themselves and leaning towards the kind you actually watch.

highlights.title: Music
highlights.body: The music section as a page of its own, next to Clips.

highlights.title: The language on the card is the language that plays
highlights.body: A title marked [Bengali] opens in Bengali, and a plain title opens in its original audio, instead of whichever copy answered quickest. Every other audio track is still one tap away.

highlights.title: Watch History plays again
highlights.body: A title from the extra library resumes straight from Watch History, including after the app has been closed and reopened.

highlights.title: More Like This is filled in
highlights.body: Titles that only the extra library carries now show genuinely related titles instead of an empty row.

highlights.title: Download sizes, and Coming Soon
highlights.body: A download says how many GB or MB it will take, and a title the library does not hold yet is marked Coming Soon on the card instead of failing when it is tapped.

highlights.title: Bengali, split properly
highlights.body: Bengali Movies, Bengali Natok and Bangladeshi Cinema are separate categories, alongside Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Punjabi, Malayalam, Kannada and English.

highlights.title: Subtitles that are really there
highlights.body: Many titles used to offer a subtitle that showed nothing: the library answers with an empty 34-byte placeholder file, and it is now recognised and ignored. When their real subtitles do not come on the first ask, they are asked for again, and a sibling copy of the same film is asked too.

highlights.title: Watch History belongs to the account
highlights.body: Signed in, what you watch is kept with your account, so another phone — or the same phone after a reinstall — carries on where you left off. Signed out, history stays on the phone only, exactly as before, and clearing it clears it everywhere.

highlights.title: VIP servers open first
highlights.body: Every title now leads with our VIP servers, so a tap starts playing instead of loading. If a VIP server is ever busy, the title keeps playing on the next server on its own.

highlights.title: Every episode of every season
highlights.body: Series carry their full run, and episode two opens as readily as episode one.

highlights.title: Search finds your language
highlights.body: Type a title and its Hindi, Bengali, Tamil and Telugu editions appear beside the original, without typing the tag.

highlights.title: Seventeen new national categories
highlights.body: Bengali Cinema, Pakistani, Nepali, Sri Lankan, Turkish, Korean, Japanese and more, each filled with that country's own films and series.

highlights.title: The main page and Categories agree
highlights.body: Every category you can open from Categories now has its own row on the main page too.

highlights.title: 18+ is yours to allow
highlights.body: Mature categories stay out of sight until you allow them on your account, and Family Mode keeps them away entirely.

highlights.title: More subtitles and more audio
highlights.body: Titles arrive with the subtitle and audio tracks their sources carry, Bengali included.

highlights.title: Fuller detail pages
highlights.body: Cast, crew, running time, certificate, stills and description on titles that had none before.

highlights.title: Back goes back
highlights.body: Leaving a category returns you to Categories, not to the top of the app.

highlights.title: One library, one set of categories
highlights.body: Every category now holds everything we can offer in it. Titles that were missing from a category are simply in it, next to the rest, and categories nobody else covers - Anime, Biography, Sport - are there too.

highlights.title: Play starts sooner, in the best picture available
highlights.body: A tap measures every server for a title at once and starts on the best one it can reach, preferring adaptive HEVC first. Films that opened blurry now open sharp.

highlights.title: A title you have never watched starts at the beginning
highlights.body: Your place in a film belongs to that film, so nothing opens part-way through by mistake.

highlights.title: Age ratings are honest
highlights.body: A certificate is shown as the certificate it is, the 18+ section holds only what belongs there, and Family Mode still keeps back anything mature or unrated.

highlights.title: The main page loads the way it always did
highlights.body: Your hero and your rows, with nothing waiting to load on top of them.

highlights.title: A much bigger library to browse, not just to search
highlights.body: Our widest library now has its own shelves on the main page and its own sections under Categories, so thousands of films, series, anime and kids titles are there to scroll through instead of only being found by typing a name.

highlights.title: Series play to the end
highlights.body: Every season and every episode a series really has is listed, including long-running shows and the newest episodes.

highlights.title: More audio languages
highlights.body: Where a title exists in several languages, all of them are offered in the audio menu, original audio first.

highlights.title: Downloads keep their place
highlights.body: A download of one of these titles stays the same download after you close the app, sign out or sign back in, and it picks up where it stopped instead of starting again.

highlights.title: 18+ stays where it belongs
highlights.body: Adult titles live behind their own entry, never on the main page, and Family Mode hides them along with anything that carries no age rating.

highlights.title: Thousands more films and series play
highlights.body: Titles from our widest library now open, stream and download like everything else in the app, in the quality they were released in and with their own audio tracks.

highlights.title: Fewer dead ends
highlights.body: When a title needs a second look, the app can go back and find it again instead of stopping at an error.

highlights.title: A cleaner player
highlights.body: Skip and speed indicators are drawn to match the rest of the app, so the picture stays the focus while you jump forward, jump back or hold for double speed.

highlights.title: A cleaner player
highlights.body: Skip and speed indicators are drawn to match the rest of the app, so the picture stays the focus while you jump forward, jump back or hold for double speed.

highlights.title: Consistent look across the app
highlights.body: Menus, filters and overlays now share one set of crisp controls on every phone and Android version.

highlights.title: More films and series open on the first tap
highlights.body: Titles from one of our largest libraries now start straight away, in 1080p, 720p or 480p, whichever your connection allows.

highlights.title: Daily serials and long-running shows, episode by episode
highlights.body: Pick any season and any episode, including the newest ones, and it plays like everything else.

highlights.title: More films and series play, in more languages
highlights.body: MovieHouse now reads one of its biggest libraries the way its own app does, so titles that had stopped playing come back, with every quality and dubbed version that library carries.

highlights.title: Swipe across the picture to move through it
highlights.body: Drag left or right anywhere on the video to scrub, see exactly where you will land before you let go, and let go to jump there.

highlights.title: Volume moves as gently as you do
highlights.body: A slow drag on the right side now changes the sound a little at a time instead of jumping several notches, and brightness on the left works the same way.

highlights.title: Fast-forward and skips you can see
highlights.body: Hold to speed up and double tap to skip, with the arrows, the count and the 2x badge drawn on screen while it happens.

highlights.title: Every result shows its own artwork
highlights.body: Titles that publish only a poster now fill the row and the header properly, so nothing looks half-loaded.

highlights.title: The home page keeps your place
highlights.body: Open a title, come back, and you are exactly where you were — the same row, the same posters, as far along as you had scrolled.

highlights.title: The download notification takes you to your downloads
highlights.body: Tap the progress notification while something is saving and MovieHouse opens on Downloads, with the film you were told about right there.

highlights.title: Choosing a download starts sooner
highlights.body: The Download panel names the server it is reading and how many it has, and it moves on quickly from one that will not answer instead of leaving you with a spinner.

highlights.title: Signing in picks up where you left off
highlights.body: Leave MovieHouse to fetch the code from your email and come back: you land on the same step, with the code you already have still valid. Nothing to start over, and no second email to wait for.

highlights.title: Every row on the home screen keeps going
highlights.body: Swipe a category and it keeps loading — the whole catalogue behind it, not the first few posters. Top 10 stays ten, the way a Top 10 should.

highlights.title: Your account is what opens a film
highlights.body: MovieHouse now checks your account before a stream starts, so nobody can use MovieHouse in your name or lean on it from outside the app. You will not notice it — films open exactly as before.

highlights.title: Nothing you already saved was touched
highlights.body: Your downloads, your list and where you stopped watching are all exactly as you left them.

highlights.title: Your download shelf follows your account
highlights.body: Sign in on another phone and MovieHouse now shows what you have downloaded elsewhere, with the quality, the size and which phone holds it. A film cannot move from one phone to another, so each row offers to download it here as well, in one tap.

highlights.title: Deleting on one phone updates the other
highlights.body: Delete a download and it stops being offered on your other phones. Downloads still keep for 30 days, and opening the app starts those 30 days again.

highlights.title: A new version no longer hides
highlights.body: When an update is ready you are told once, you can say Later, and it waits for you in Settings until you want it. Nothing forces you out of what you were watching.

highlights.title: Nothing you already saved was touched
highlights.body: Every download already on your phone stays exactly where it was and plays the same offline.

highlights.title: Your downloads belong to your account
highlights.body: Sign out and sign back in and your saved films are all there. If someone else signs in on the same phone, they see their own downloads and not yours.

highlights.title: Downloads now keep for 30 days
highlights.body: A finished download keeps for 30 days, and opening MovieHouse starts those 30 days again. The shelf tells you how long is left, and a film you never come back for gives its space back to your phone.

highlights.title: Use mobile data when you want to
highlights.body: Wi-Fi only is still the default so no data is spent by surprise. Now you can switch to mobile data right where you start a download, or on a download that is waiting for Wi-Fi.

highlights.title: Nothing you already saved was touched
highlights.body: Everything that was on your phone before this update is still there, exactly as it was, and it plays the same offline.

highlights.title: Download any episode you like
highlights.body: Every episode in a season now has its own Download button, so you take the ones you want and nothing else.

highlights.title: See the speed and the time left
highlights.body: A download tells you how fast it is going and how long is left, updated every second while it runs.

highlights.title: Know your room before you start
highlights.body: MovieHouse shows how much space is free on your phone, and says so plainly when a film will not fit.

highlights.title: The home page keeps your place
highlights.body: Open a title, watch something, come back — the home page is exactly where you left it instead of jumping to the top.

highlights.title: Your downloads stay when you sign out
highlights.body: Sign out and sign back in and everything you saved is still in Downloads, ready to play — nothing to fetch again.

highlights.title: Saved is saved for good
highlights.body: A download never expires on its own. It stays on your phone until you choose to delete it, and one tap removes it.

highlights.title: Pick the audio language you want
highlights.body: Choose the language before a download starts, and switch between the languages a title carries while you watch.

highlights.title: Watch with nothing connected
highlights.body: Anything you have saved plays straight from your phone, with the audio you picked, even in flight mode.

highlights.title: Pause, carry on, or delete
highlights.body: Stop a download and pick it up later where it stopped, and Wi-Fi only waits by itself until Wi-Fi is back.

highlights.title: Downloads, for real
highlights.body: Press Download on any film or episode, choose the quality and the language you want, and MovieHouse saves it on your phone.

highlights.title: Watch with no connection at all
highlights.body: Anything you have saved plays straight from your phone, with the audio you picked, even in flight mode.

highlights.title: Every language the film really has
highlights.body: The Audio button now lists all of them in one place, including the ones that live on another server, and switches you over at the same second.

highlights.title: You can see exactly where a download is
highlights.body: Real percentage, real size, and Pause and Resume whenever you like.

highlights.title: Wi-Fi only means Wi-Fi only
highlights.body: Downloads wait for Wi-Fi when you ask them to, and carry on by themselves the moment it is back.

highlights.title: One phone stays one phone
highlights.body: Reinstalling MovieHouse no longer eats a device slot, so a correct password never gets stopped by "already on 3 devices" again.

highlights.title: Out of device slots? Free one here
highlights.body: If your plan's devices are all in use, the sign-in screen now lists them and lets you remove the one you no longer use.

highlights.title: One thing per step
highlights.body: Choosing a password and typing the emailed code are separate steps now, and forgotten passwords ask for the code first.

highlights.title: Buttons wait for you
highlights.body: Continue stays switched off until your password meets every rule, both fields match, and the code is all six digits.

highlights.title: Set your password without losing your place
highlights.body: If you were already signed in, the password box now opens over the screen you were on instead of taking over the app.

highlights.title: One screen for signing in and signing up
highlights.body: Type your email and MovieHouse takes you to the right step by itself. New here? Choose a password and confirm your email once. Coming back? Your password is all it takes.

highlights.title: See your password while you type it
highlights.body: Tap the eye to show or hide it, watch each rule tick off as you type, and see how strong your password is before you save it.

highlights.title: Forgot your password?
highlights.body: Ask for a 6-digit code, then choose a new password right there and you are back in.

highlights.title: No more waiting for email codes
highlights.body: Your password gets you in on any phone, so a code is only ever needed to create your account or to reset your password.

highlights.title: Video fills the whole screen
highlights.body: Nothing sits above the picture any more on Android 12 and newer — the frame runs edge to edge.

highlights.title: Sign in with a password
highlights.body: Set a password once, and this phone takes you straight in — no waiting for an email code. Forgot it? A 6-digit code still gets you back, and you can set a new password right after.

highlights.title: Lock MovieHouse when you step away
highlights.body: Lock the app from Settings, or ask for your password every time MovieHouse opens, so nobody else can open your account on your phone.

highlights.title: Fewer sign-in emails
highlights.body: Asking for a new code now waits a little longer each time, so your inbox stays clean and the code you have is always the newest one.

highlights.title: Playback speed, 0.25x to 2x
highlights.body: Open Speed in the player to slow a scene down or move through it faster. Your choice carries over to the next title, and a press-and-hold skims ahead at any time.

highlights.title: Choose your audio language
highlights.body: The player now lists every audio track a title actually includes — with 5.1, 7.1 and Dolby marked — so you can see what a film offers before you pick.

highlights.title: Every gesture, in five seconds
highlights.body: The first time you start watching, a short on-screen guide shows you how to skip, speed up, set brightness and volume, and zoom the picture.

highlights.title: Stronger protection for your account
highlights.body: Signing out now clears your session everywhere in the app, and staying signed in means fewer verification emails.

highlights.title: Updates you can follow, and help when you need it
highlights.body: Every release now arrives with the screens it changed, and our Telegram and Facebook sit in Settings whenever you want to reach the team.

highlights.title: The picture fills your screen
highlights.body: Titles that arrive with black bars around them are detected and cropped to your screen, with nothing cut off.

highlights.title: Nothing over the picture
highlights.body: The strip that covered the top of the video on newer Android versions is gone.
